'''Gujarat State Fertilizers & Chemicals Limited (GSFC)''' is a publicly-traded Indian chemicals and fertilizers manufacturer, partly owned by the [[Government of Gujarat]]. GSFC was founded in 1962 and has its headquarters in [[Vadodara]] on the [[Ahmedabad Vadodara Expressway]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gsfclimited.com/secretarial.asp?mnuid=5|title=Financial Detail – Investor's Grievance Redressal|website=www.gsfclimited.com|access-date=2016-09-26}}</ref> As of fiscal year 2021–22, fertilizers such as [[diammonium phosphate]], [[ammonium sulfate]] and [[urea]] generated over 60% of the company's revenue, while industrial products including [[caprolactam]], [[nylon 6]], [[melamine]] and [[Methylethyl ketone oxime|MEK oxime]] contributed the remaining share.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gujarat State Fertilizers & Chemicals Limited |url=https://www.careratings.com/upload/CompanyFiles/PR/27092022060901_Gujarat_State_Fertilizers_&_Chemicals_Limited.pdf |access-date=28 February 2023 |work=CARE Ratings}}</ref>

Oil and gas discovered in [[Bombay High]] and South Basin triggered the birth of 8 new generation fertilizer plants to fulfill the growing food needs of India. In 1976, it set up a plant in [[Bharuch]] which trades as [[Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilisers & Chemicals]], as a [[subsidiary]] of GSFC.

In 2012, GSFC incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary called GSFC AgroTech Limited (GATL).<ref>{{cite news |title=GSFC Agrotech Limited |url=https://www.careratings.com/upload/CompanyFiles/PR/04102022073640_GSFC_Agrotech_Limited.pdf |access-date=28 February 2023 |work=CARE Ratings}}</ref>

In 2015, GSFC helped start GSFC University in Vadodara, Gujarat.<ref>{{cite news
 |title=GSFC to set up university in Vadodara
 |author=Press Trust of India
 |newspaper=Business Standard
 |date=2 August 2015
 |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/gsfc-to-set-up-university-in-vadodara-115080200326_1.html
 |access-date=30 December 2025
}}</ref>
